summary: Frontend-only retest after custom CSS 3D Flipbook replaced react-pageflip. FULL editor flow now works end-to-end: signup → wizard (template + A5/landscape + details + 3 JPGs) → AI processing → editor renders with all controls. All required data-testids exist and are functional. Prev/Next flip the spread and 'Double-page X' indicator updates (1→2→1). 'Ajouter texte' inserts a text item on the right content page and opens the edit panel with font/color/size controls. Font select and size range update the text live (verified Manrope + 48px). Enregistrer → PATCH /api/albums/{id} returns 200. Export PDF opens a new tab and GET /api/albums/{id}/export returns 200 application/pdf. No blank-page crash, no React 19 insertBefore errors.

issues: The first content spread showed the same photo (food.jpg) rendered on the left as a 'text' item ('food') instead of as an image — appears to be the layout template treating the caption item. Cosmetic: the added 'Votre légende' text overflows the right page bounds at 48px (it visually spills onto the seam between pages). Consider clamping font_size given the item's bounding box (w=0.6, h=0.08) or auto-shrinking to fit.

action_items: (Optional cosmetic) In AlbumEditor.jsx, clamp or auto-shrink text items when font_size exceeds the item's bounding box height so large sizes don't overflow the page seam.

(Optional) In the Playwright automation, opening a PDF response in a new tab never fires domcontentloaded (browser download UI) — main agent can safely rely on window.open(pdf_url); no code change required.
critical_code_review_comments: Flipbook.jsx (new) is clean, React-19-safe, and correctly exposes ref.pageFlip().flipNext/flipPrev for API-compatibility with the previous library. No error boundary is still present, but the custom implementation has no third-party crash surface.

AlbumEditor.jsx addTextToCurrentPage maps spread index → content page index via '(pageIndex * 2) - 1'. When pageIndex=1 (first content spread) it targets content page 0 (right page of the pair since spread 1 = cover-front + first content page). Verified visually: text lands on the right side. LGTM.

BookRenderer builds pages array with cover-front + blank + content pages + blank + cover-back. Total pages = content+3 (odd if content is even), so last spread may end with the back cover on the left and a phantom blank on the right — not a bug, just noted.
editorColorInput native <input type='color'> works but is only 24×24px and easy to miss; consider a tooltip. Non-blocking.

success_rate.backend: n/a (skipped this round per request; was 100% previously)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of required editor flows (5/5 testids present, prev/next flip, add-text, font/color/size, save 200, export PDF 200 application/pdf)

test_credentials: Signup created fresh accounts: TEST_ui_<uuid>@fable.studio / Test1234! (login flow via /api/auth/signup then Bearer token).
seed_data_creation: Created one user + one A5 landscape album with 3 JPGs (food.jpg, landscape.jpg, portrait.jpg from /tmp/testimgs). Album status went processing → ready in ~6s. A second smaller album was created via API to independently verify the PDF endpoint (200, application/pdf, 2277 bytes).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix for react-pageflip crash is verified working. Custom Flipbook in /app/frontend/src/components/Flipbook.jsx uses CSS 3D animation (700ms) — always sleep ~1s between flipNext/flipPrev clicks before reading the 'Double-page X' indicator. Editor processing typically resolves within 6-10s but poll up to 90s. Photo input at [data-testid='photo-input'] is display:hidden; use page.set_input_files without waiting for visibility. PDF export opens a new tab whose response is application/pdf → new_page.wait_for_load_state may time out; verify PDF via a direct GET to /api/albums/{id}/export?auth=<token> instead.
rca of the issue: Previous iteration's blank editor was caused by react-pageflip 2.0.3 direct-DOM insertBefore incompatibility with React 19. Root cause resolved by replacing it with a custom React-19-native CSS 3D flipbook component (Flipbook.jsx) that keeps the same imperative ref API (ref.pageFlip().flipNext/flipPrev). No more pageerrors, no more unmount, all editor controls mount and are interactive.
